# Rules

The rule books, the definitions, and the folders that hold them. This page holds the full text of the live definitions of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

<a id="d-05"></a>

## D-05: Registered definition `[STABLE]`

> A definition that lives in the `entries/` folder of a definition folder and appears in its index.

A registered definition lives in a definition folder, as `entries/<ID>.md`, and appears in the index of that folder, its `README.md`. [The `reg-definitions` skill](../../../../.claude/skills/reg-definitions/SKILL.md) gives its format, and it passes `generate-index.mjs --check`.

A registered definition has an ID that never changes, aliases that the script checks, and one place where every reader finds it. It wins over every loose definition of the same term. [R-06](../../rules/entries/R-06.md) gives the rule.

<a id="d-06"></a>

## D-06: Loose definition `[STABLE]`

> A definition that explains a term only where the term is used, outside any definition folder.

A loose definition explains a term only where the term is used, for example in a sentence of a rule or in a code comment. It has no ID, and no script checks it.

Loose definitions are allowed. A loose definition never contradicts a registered definition of the same term. If the two disagree, the registered definition holds, and the loose one is the text to fix. To give a registered term another meaning, change its registered definition with the `reg-definitions` skill instead of redefining it locally. [R-06](../../rules/entries/R-06.md) gives the rule.

<a id="d-07"></a>

## D-07: Definition folder `[STABLE]`

> A registry folder, usually named `definitions/`, that holds registered definitions.

Aliases: definitions folder.

A definition folder is a registry folder whose `README.md` declares `kind: definitions`. Its `entries/` folder holds one file per registered definition, named `<ID>.md`, its `README.md` indexes them, and its `groups/` folder holds the generated group pages. For example, `global/definitions/` holds the global definitions, from `entries/D-01.md` on.

Every file in the `entries/` folder of a definition folder is a registered definition. [The `reg-definitions` skill](../../../../.claude/skills/reg-definitions/SKILL.md) gives the format of the files, and `generate-index.mjs` checks them.

<a id="d-08"></a>

## D-08: Rule folder `[STABLE]`

> A registry folder of the kind `rules`, usually named `rules/`, that holds one rule book.

Aliases: rules folder.

A rule folder is a registry folder whose `README.md` declares `kind: rules`. Its `entries/` folder holds one file per rule, named after the ID of the rule, its `README.md` indexes them, and its `groups/` folder holds the generated group pages. For example, `global/rules/` holds the global rules, from `entries/R-01.md` on.

[The `reg-rules` skill](../../../../.claude/skills/reg-rules/SKILL.md) gives the fields of a rule, and [the `reg` skill](../../../../.claude/skills/reg/SKILL.md) gives the layout and the script.

A rule book not converted yet keeps its rules in topic files, next to a `rules.md` that indexes them, as `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/rules/` does today.

<a id="d-09"></a>

## D-09: Definition tag `[STABLE]`

> The tag in the front matter of a registered definition that says whether the definition can change or is retired.

A definition tag sits in the `tag` field of the front matter of each registered definition. It says whether the definition can change, and whether the definition is still in use.

[`TAGS.json`](../../../../.claude/skills/reg-definitions/TAGS.json), in the folder of the `reg-definitions` skill, lists the definition tags and their meanings. It is the only list. Every generated index, such as [README.md](../README.md), shows it as a table.

A definition tag is not a rule tag. A rule tag says whether a rule and the code agree. Write "definition tag" or "rule tag" wherever "tag" alone could mean either.

<a id="d-10"></a>

## D-10: Rule tag `[STABLE]`

> The tag of a rule that says whether the rule text and the code agree.

Aliases: status tag.

A rule tag sits in the `tag` field of the front matter of each rule. It says whether the rule text is accurate, whether the code follows it, and whether a check enforces it.

[`TAGS.json`](../../../../.claude/skills/reg-rules/TAGS.json), in the folder of the `reg-rules` skill, lists the rule tags and their meanings. It is the only list.

A rule tag is not a definition tag. A definition tag says whether a definition can change or is retired. Write "definition tag" or "rule tag" wherever "tag" alone could mean either.

<a id="d-11"></a>

## D-11: Registry folder `[STABLE]`

> A folder that holds one kind of entry, such as definitions or rules, with a generated index, one file per entry, and generated group pages.

Aliases: registry.

A registry folder holds one kind of entry. Its layout is the same for every kind:

- `README.md`: the index. Its front matter names the kind and the ID prefix and declares any groups. The script `generate-index.mjs` of [the `reg` skill](../../../../.claude/skills/reg/SKILL.md) generates the part between its two markers.
- `entries/`: one file per entry, named after its ID, as in `entries/D-02.md`. The front matter of each file holds the data of the entry.
- `groups/`: the generated pages, one per group, and `all.md` with every live entry.

The kind sets the letter of the IDs, the fields of an entry, and the list of tags. A definition folder is a registry folder of the kind `definitions`.
